text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.

- Finland must not be left offside in its relationship with NATO, says Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen. Says if Russia achieves influence on NATO, Finland should get similar: but repeats Finland is not seeking membership.
- Official paper recycling targets are too high since part of Finland's rapidly growing exports of paper products to Russia remain in Finland's consumption statistics, paper industry says.
- Josef Stalin said in 1940 after the Winter War that Finland's military defence was passive and its offence clumsy, according to a newly-found copy of a speech.
- The state, which owns shares worth about 70 billion markka, plans to raise six billion through privatisation in 1997 to 1999.

- Foreign investors who speculated that the markka would strengthen early this year are now trapped with some 25 billion to 30 billion markka and since the markka has not moved much, can anticipate little profit, analysts say.
- In a year and a half, companies will be able to deliver annual reports electronically to the patent and register authority, official says.
- Swedish power utility Vattenfall says is still interested in Finnish Savon Voima but is not planning to make an offer.
- Justice ministry is considering proposals to allow a police register of DNA from people convicted or suspected of serious criminal offences.
